literal: When Zong surrendered the city to the state, Zong's chief clerk Jiang Ge, marshal Zu Yang, and five thousand soldiers and officers were all captured.
idiomatic: When Zong turned the city over to Wei, his chief clerk Jiang Ge, marshal Zu Yang, and five thousand troops were taken captive.

literal: Emperor Suzong ordered the authorities to send Ge and the others entirely back south, and thereby summon Lue.
idiomatic: Suzong ordered the court to return Ge and the rest to the south and to summon Lue home.

literal: Yan then prepared full rites and sent him off.
idiomatic: Yan then sent him away with full ceremony.

literal: When Lue was about to return, Yan set out wine for a farewell feast, bestowed a hundred jin of gold and silver, and all of Yan's hundred officials escorted him to the riverbank; he sent his Right Guard Xu Que with more than a hundred men to escort him to the capital.
idiomatic: As Lue prepared to leave, Yan gave a farewell feast and a hundred jin of gold and silver; every Liang minister saw him off on the river, and Xu Que of the Right Guard led a hundred men to escort him to the capital.

literal: An edict made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Diao Shuang go to the border to greet and inquire after him; another edict granted Xuzhou a thousand bolts each of silk and cloth.
idiomatic: Suzong sent Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Diao Shuang to the frontier to welcome him and ordered a thousand bolts each of silk and cloth for Xuzhou.

literal: Lue was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Prince of Yiyang with a fief of a thousand households.
idiomatic: He was named attendant-in-ordinary and prince of Yiyang with a thousand-household fief.

literal: On reaching Shiren post station, an edict allowed kinsmen of the imperial clan, relatives, and all inner and outer officials who knew him beforehand to go to the near suburbs to welcome him.
idiomatic: At Shiren post station an edict let clan kin, relatives, and any courtier who already knew him meet him in the near suburbs.

literal: He was granted three thousand bolts of silk, one residence, five thousand shi of grain, and thirty slaves.
idiomatic: He received three thousand bolts of silk, a mansion, five thousand shi of grain, and thirty slaves.

literal: His former marshal Shi Bin was made Supervising Attendant and led the Straight Rear; Li Faguang was made magistrate of his home county; Diao Chang was made Administrator of Dongping; Diao Shuang was made Inspector of Western Yanzhou.
idiomatic: His old marshal Shi Bin became supervising attendant and led the Straight Rear; Li Faguang became his home-county magistrate; Diao Chang became Dongping administrator; Diao Shuang became Western Yanzhou inspector.

literal: Every place Lue had stayed even a single meal or a single night received rewards without exception.
idiomatic: Every inn or house that had fed or lodged him even once was showered with gifts.

literal: Soon his fief was changed to Prince of Dongping; he was also made General of Chariots and Cavalry, Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, and Commander of the Left Guard, Attendant-in-Ordinary as before.
idiomatic: Soon he was re-created prince of Dongping and named general of chariots and cavalry, left grand master of splendid happiness, equal in honor to the three dukes, and commander of the left guard while keeping attendant-in-ordinary.

literal: He also retained his original office as Director of the National University and was transferred to Great General and Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He kept the national university directorship and was promoted to great general and director of the masters of writing.

literal: [4] The Empress Dowager Ling greatly favored and trusted him; the trust placed in him was nearly on a par with Yuan Hui.
idiomatic: [4] Empress Dowager Ling doted on him; her trust in him nearly matched Yuan Hui's.

literal: At that time the realm had many troubles and military and state affairs were myriad; Lue kept to routine and protected himself, with no other benefit—only a compliant minister.
idiomatic: The realm was in turmoil and state and army affairs endless; Lue held to routine, looked after himself, and offered nothing beyond a yes-man's compliance.

literal: Erzhu Rong was Lue's uncle by marriage, whom Lue had always slighted; Lue also sided with Zheng Yan and Xu He, and Rong harbored resentment on both counts.
idiomatic: Erzhu Rong was his uncle by marriage and a man he had long despised; Lue also backed Zheng Yan and Xu He, and Rong hated him twice over.

literal: When Rong entered Luoyang, Lue was killed at Heyin.
idiomatic: When Rong took Luoyang, Lue died in the Heyin massacre.

literal: Posthumously he was given his former offices plus Grand Guardian, Minister of Works, and Inspector of Xuzhou; posthumous title: Wen Zhen.
idiomatic: Posthumously he kept his ranks and was added grand guardian, minister of works, and Xuzhou inspector, styled Wen Zhen.

literal: His son Jingshi inherited.
idiomatic: His son Jingshi succeeded.

literal: In the Wuding era he was Administrator of Northern Guangping.
idiomatic: Under Wuding he governed Northern Guangping.

literal: When Qi received the Mandate, titles were reduced by precedent.
idiomatic: After Qi took the throne, enfeoffments were lowered by precedent.

literal: Lue's younger brother Zuan
idiomatic: Lue's younger brother Zuan

literal: (Appended son: Zixian)
idiomatic: (Appended son: Zixian)

literal: Lue's younger brother Zuan, styled Shaoxing, had considerable military talent.
idiomatic: Lue's younger brother Zuan, styled Shaoxing, showed real talent in war.

literal: He was made Libationer of the Ministry of Rites.
idiomatic: He served as libationer of the ministry of rites.

literal: On hearing that Xi had raised troops, he fled to Ye and was seized on arrival; he died together with Xi.
idiomatic: When Xi rose in arms he fled to Ye, was seized at once, and died with him.

literal: Posthumously he was enfeoffed as Duke of Beiping County, given in gift General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Hengzhou, changed to Marquis Who Founded the State of Gaotang with a fief of eight hundred households.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was made duke of Beiping county and given general who pacifies the north and Hengzhou inspector, then re-created founding marquis of Gaotang with eight hundred households.

literal: His son Zixian inherited.
idiomatic: His son Zixian succeeded.

literal: He died as Vice Director of Jingzhou.
idiomatic: He died as Jingzhou vice director.

literal: Xi's younger brother by a different mother, Prince of Wuyi Yixing
idiomatic: Xi's younger half-brother, Prince of Wuyi Yixing

literal: (Appended son: Shu)
idiomatic: (Appended son: Shu)

literal: Xi's younger brother by a different mother, Yixing, was given in adoption to his paternal uncle Bingluo.
idiomatic: Xi's half-brother Yixing was adopted by their uncle Bingluo.

literal: At the beginning of Suzong's reign he was made Outer Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary Service.
idiomatic: Early in Suzong's reign he was made outer attendant cavalier in ordinary service.

literal: When Xi met disaster, Yixing, because he had been given out in adoption, was therefore not implicated.
idiomatic: When Xi was destroyed, Yixing escaped punishment because he had been adopted away.

literal: He was gradually transferred to General Who Assists the State and Regular Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary Service.
idiomatic: He rose to general who assists the state and regular attendant cavalier in ordinary service.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was killed at Heyin.
idiomatic: Early in Xiaozhuang's reign he died at Heyin.

literal: Posthumously he was given General of the Central Army and Inspector of Yingzhou.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was named general of the central army and Yingzhou inspector.

literal: Later he was posthumously given Regular Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary Service and General Who Pacifies the East; the rest as before.
idiomatic: Later he was also given regular attendant cavalier in ordinary service and general who pacifies the east; other ranks unchanged.

literal: Yixing's wife was Lady Li of Zhao commandery.
idiomatic: Yixing's wife was Lady Li of Zhao commandery.

literal: Li was skilled in women's crafts and was intimate with Erzhu Rong's wife.
idiomatic: Lady Li was skilled in women's crafts and close to Erzhu Rong's wife.

literal: In the Yong'an era Yixing was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yan commandery with a fief of five hundred households; soon changed to Prince of Julu, then again to Prince of Wuyi.
idiomatic: In Yong'an Yixing was posthumously made prince of Yan commandery with five hundred households, then prince of Julu, then prince of Wuyi.

literal: His son Shu inherited.
idiomatic: His son Shu succeeded.

literal: In the Tianping era he was Regular Attendant.
idiomatic: Under Tianping he was regular attendant.

literal: When Qi received the Mandate, titles were reduced by precedent.
idiomatic: After Qi took the throne, enfeoffments were lowered by precedent.

literal: Prince of Fufeng Yi
idiomatic: Prince of Fufeng Yi

literal: Ying's younger brother Yi began as Commandant of Footsoldiers, transferred to Commandant of the City Gates, and was made General of Shanshan Garrison.
idiomatic: Ying's younger brother Yi rose from footsoldier commandant to city-gate commandant and then Shanshan garrison general.

literal: Wherever he served he was greedy and violent; the authorities impeached him, but he fled and escaped punishment.
idiomatic: Every post found him greedy and brutal; impeached, he fled and escaped.

literal: In the Yan chang era he died.
idiomatic: He died in the Yanchang era.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, because he was Erzhu Rong's brother-in-law, he was posthumously promoted to General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Duke, Inspector of Yongzhou, and Prince of Fufeng.
idiomatic: Early in Xiaozhuang's reign, as Erzhu Rong's brother-in-law, he was posthumously raised to general of agile cavalry, grand duke, Yongzhou inspector, and prince of Fufeng.

literal: Son: Prince of Lu Su
idiomatic: Son: Prince of Lu Su

literal: (Appended son: Daoyu)
idiomatic: (Appended son: Daoyu)

literal: His son Daoyu inherited.
idiomatic: His son Daoyu succeeded.

literal: He was made General of the Van.
idiomatic: He was named general of the van.

literal: When Qi received the Mandate, titles were reduced by precedent.
idiomatic: After Qi took the throne, enfeoffments were lowered by precedent.

literal: Prince of Donghai Ye
idiomatic: Prince of Donghai Ye

literal: Ye, styled Huaxing, childhood name Penzi.
idiomatic: Ye, styled Huaxing, childhood name Penzi.

literal: By nature he was frivolous and rash, with great physical strength.
idiomatic: He was frivolous and rash, with uncommon strength.

literal: He began as Secretary, and was gradually transferred to Regular Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary Service.
idiomatic: He began in the secretariat and rose to regular attendant cavalier in ordinary service.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was enfeoffed as Prince of Changguang with a fief of a thousand households.
idiomatic: Early in Xiaozhuang's reign he was made prince of Changguang with a thousand households.

literal: He went out as Administrator of Taiyuan and acted as commissioner for Bingzhou affairs.
idiomatic: He went out as Taiyuan administrator and acting Bingzhou commissioner.

literal: When Erzhu Rong died, Shilong and the others fled back to Bingzhou, met Erzhu Zhao at Jianxing, and there set up Ye as ruler, proclaimed a general amnesty in their territory, and took the reign title Jianming.
idiomatic: After Erzhu Rong's death Shilong fled to Bingzhou, joined Erzhu Zhao at Jianxing, set Ye on the throne, amnestied their command, and declared the Jianming era.

literal: Soon he was deposed by Shilong and the others.
idiomatic: Soon Shilong and his party deposed him.

literal: When the Former Deposed Emperor was enthroned, Ye was enfeoffed as Prince of Donghai with a fief of ten thousand households.
idiomatic: When the former deposed emperor took the throne, Ye was made prince of Donghai with ten thousand households.

literal: At the beginning of the Deposed Emperor's reign, for an offense he was granted death in his residence.
idiomatic: Early in the Deposed Emperor's reign he was sentenced to death in his own house.

literal: He had no son; the fief was abolished.
idiomatic: He left no heir and the fief was extinguished.

literal: Prince Kang of Chengyang Changshou
idiomatic: Prince Kang of Chengyang Changshou

literal: Prince of Chengyang Changshou was enfeoffed in the second year of Huangxing and made General Who Pacifies the West and Grand Director of the Outer Court.
idiomatic: Changshou was enfeoffed prince of Chengyang in Huangxing year 2 and named general who pacifies the west and grand director of the outer court.

literal: He went out as Grand General of Woye Garrison.
idiomatic: He went out as grand general of Woye garrison.

literal: By nature he was clever and skilled at winning people; at his post he had great prestige.
idiomatic: Clever and skilled at winning men, he held great authority in his command.

literal: In the fifth year of Yanxing he died; posthumous title: Prince Kang.
idiomatic: He died in Yanxing year 5 and was posthumously styled Kang.

literal: Eldest son: Duohou
idiomatic: Eldest son: Duohou

literal: The eldest son Duohou died young.
idiomatic: The eldest son Duohou died young.

literal: Second son: Prince Huai of Chengyang Luan
idiomatic: Second son: Prince Huai of Chengyang Luan

literal: The second son Luan, styled Xuanming.
idiomatic: The second son Luan, styled Xuanming.

literal: At first he succeeded his uncle, Prince Jing of Zhangwu; when his elder brother died he returned to inherit his father's title.
idiomatic: He first succeeded his uncle, Prince Jing of Zhangwu; when his brother died he returned to his father's fief.

literal: His body was eight chi tall, his belt ten wei around; he was famed for martial skill.
idiomatic: Eight chi tall, with a ten-wei belt, he was famed for martial prowess.

literal: Repeatedly he was made Grand General of the Northern Capital.
idiomatic: He was repeatedly named grand general of the northern capital.

literal: [5] In Gaozu's time he was made Grand Director of the Outer Court, then went out as Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all military affairs in Hexi, General Who Pacifies the West, concurrent Protector of the Western Rong, and Grand General of Liangzhou Garrison.
idiomatic: [5] Under Gaozu he became grand director of the outer court, then bearer of the staff, commander of Hexi, general who pacifies the west, protector of the western Rong, and Liangzhou garrison grand general.

literal: The garrison was changed to establish a province; Luan was made Inspector of Liangzhou and Grand General of Guzang Garrison; the rest as before.
idiomatic: The garrison became a province; Luan was made Liangzhou inspector and Guzang garrison grand general, other ranks unchanged.

literal: Later he came to court at the capital.
idiomatic: Later he came to court.

literal: When the imperial carriage marched south on campaign, he was made General Who Stabilizes the Army.
idiomatic: When the emperor marched south on campaign, he was named general who stabilizes the army.

literal: When the capital was fixed at Luoyang, Gaozu visited Ye and ordered Luan to remain on guard.
idiomatic: When the capital was set at Luoyang, Gaozu went to Ye and left Luan to hold the city.

literal: Then the five ranks of enfeoffment were established; his fief was a thousand households.
idiomatic: When the five ranks were instituted his fief stood at a thousand households.

literal: He was made Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the South, Commander of military affairs in Yu, Jing, and Ying provinces and in Henei, Shanyang, and Dong commanderies; with General Who Pacifies the South Lu Yuan and Li Zuo he attacked Zheyang, failed to take it, was defeated, and withdrew.
idiomatic: He was bearer of the staff, general who pacifies the south, and commander of Yu, Jing, and Ying and of Henei, Shanyang, and Dong; with Lu Yuan and Li Zuo he attacked Zheyang, failed, and retreated beaten.

literal: At that time Gaozu was at Xiaqiu; Luan requested to come to the traveling palace to accept punishment.
idiomatic: Gaozu was then at Xiaqiu; Luan asked to come to the field palace and accept punishment.

literal: Gaozu summoned Luan and the others and reproached them, saying: "You lead troops in mass; by right you should exert your utmost loyalty, yet advancing you could not storm the rebel city, retreating you could not destroy this petty bandit—you have diminished royal majesty and the crime deserves execution.
idiomatic: Gaozu received Luan and the rest and rebuked them: "You commanded armies and owed the utmost loyalty; yet you could neither take the rebel city nor crush this petty foe—you have shamed the throne and deserve death.

literal: At the beginning of my reform I act from leniency; now I spare you death; Prince of Chengyang is reduced to Prince of Dingxiang County with five hundred households cut from the fief.
idiomatic: At the start of my reforms I show mercy; I spare your lives; the prince of Chengyang is reduced to prince of Dingxiang county and loses five hundred households.

literal: In antiquity, on campaign one carried the spirit-tablets of the ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain to show that authority and favor each had their proper place; now I summon your crime of the defeated army before the spirit-tablets to make your guilt manifest.
idiomatic: Antiquity required temple tablets and altar spirits on campaign to show where authority and mercy lay; I now call your defeat before those spirits to expose your fault.

literal: " Later, for his merit in remaining on guard, his original fief was restored and two hundred households were added.
idiomatic: " Later, for holding the capital, his original title was restored and two hundred households added.

literal: He was made General Who Overcomes the Enemy and Administrator of Henei, then transferred to Inspector of Bingzhou.
idiomatic: He was named general who overcomes the enemy and Henei administrator, then Bingzhou inspector.

literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign he was made General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qingzhou.
idiomatic: Early in Shizong's reign he became general who pacifies the east and Qingzhou inspector.

literal: Later he was transferred to General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Dingzhou.
idiomatic: Later he was made general who pacifies the north and Dingzhou inspector.

literal: Luan loved and delighted in Buddhism and the Way; he kept the five precepts, did not drink wine or eat meat, and for years observed long fasts.
idiomatic: Luan loved Buddhism; he kept the five precepts, ate no meat and drank no wine, and fasted for years.

literal: He built Buddhist temples, urged the common people, and together imposed labor in earth and timber—public and private expenses were disturbed, and he became a real affliction to the people.
idiomatic: He raised temples, pressed the people into earth-and-timber labor, and harassed public and private purse alike until he was a plague on the land.

literal: When Shizong heard of it he issued an edict saying: "Luan is close kin of the imperial clan and governs a great province where the people are numerous; keeping the people at peace is his charge—he ought to restrain himself and show sincere devotion, honor purity and plant kindness, yet he has repeatedly called up labor and devoted himself solely to harassment; registered households cry out and every family harbors lament.
idiomatic: Shizong heard and edicted: "Luan is imperial kin governing a populous province; his charge is peace, yet he has repeatedly conscripted labor for temples alone; households wail and every family grieves.

literal: The northern provinces are broad in territory and disorder springs from this; by the law his faults should be found and he should be sternly removed.
idiomatic: The north is vast and disorder breeds there; by law his faults warrant dismissal.

literal: Because Luan is a kinsman, affection withholds full punishment; an envoy may be sent to reprove him in the name of righteousness, and his salary may be withheld for one cycle as a slight display of penalty."
idiomatic: As kin, I spare him full disgrace; send an envoy to rebuke him and withhold one year's salary as a token punishment."

literal: In the second year of Zhengshi he died, aged thirty-eight.
idiomatic: He died in Zhengshi year 2, aged thirty-eight.

literal: Six hundred bolts of silk were granted in gift; an edict ordered Secretariat Attendant Wang Yun to proclaim the imperial message at the mourning; he was posthumously given General Who Guards the North and Inspector of Jizhou; posthumous title: Prince Huai.
idiomatic: Six hundred bolts of silk were granted; Wang Yun of the secretariat was sent to announce the throne's condolences; posthumously he was general who guards the north and Jizhou inspector, styled Huai.

literal: Son: Prince Wenxian of Chengyang Hui
idiomatic: Son: Prince Wenxian of Chengyang Hui

literal: (Appended son: Yan)
idiomatic: (Appended son: Yan)
